findings.title: Date-object identity comparison makes the zero-length override check dead code
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two distinct Dayjs objects with `===`, which is always false. The intended check (override start equals end, i.e. an empty override) never fires. Compare with `.isSame(...)` or compare `.valueOf()` instead.

findings.title: Any same-day date override makes a slot available and skips all busy-time checks
findings.body: When any date override exists on the slot's day and the slot is not rejected by the override range checks, `dateOverrideExist` is set and the function returns `true` before evaluating `busy`. A slot that overlaps a calendar event or existing booking for a fixed host is therefore reported as available, which is the exact double-booking the PR is meant to prevent.

findings.title: Working-hours check rejects slots that are inside a valid working-hours range
findings.body: `workingHours.find(...)` returns truthy if any working-hour entry for the weekday does not contain the slot. With multiple ranges per day (e.g. split shifts, or the aggregate of several users), a slot inside one range is still rejected because another range does not contain it. The check should be `!workingHours.some(...)` over ranges that contain the slot.

findings.title: Slot end minutes computed from slotStartTime, so the end bound check is meaningless
findings.body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` uses the start time, so `start` and `end` are identical. The `end > workingHour.endTime` comparison therefore only tests the slot start and never the slot's end. It should use `slotEndTime`. Slots that start inside working hours but run past the end are accepted.

findings.title: Date override range checks ignore the override's own end for the day's boundary
findings.body: The override matching logic only tests the day of `date.start` against the slot start day. Overrides that span midnight or where the slot start is on the same calendar day in the organizer timezone but the slot is on a different day in the invitee's timezone are handled inconsistently, because the UTC offset is applied to `date.start` and `date.end` but the comparison day is taken from the UTC slot time. This can match the wrong day for invitees far from the organizer timezone.

findings.title: Override offset computed by round-tripping Date through toString() loses precision and depends on server TZ
findings.body: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` formats the Date as a local-time string with seconds precision and then parses it again in the process's local timezone. Milliseconds are dropped and the result depends on the server/browser timezone, so the computed offset can be wrong. Use `dayjs(override.start)` directly. Also `override.timeZone` is optional in `TimeRange` but is passed straight to `.tz()` without a fallback, so a missing timezone silently changes the result.

findings.title: Offset sign and day-matching logic for overrides is hard to verify and inconsistent with lib/slots.ts
findings.body: `checkIfIsAvailable` computes the override offset as `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1`, while `lib/slots.ts` computes an offset as invitee-minus-organizer. The two use different conventions for the same override, which makes the shifted override windows in the two code paths disagree and is a likely source of the timezone bug the PR claims to fix.

findings.title: New timezone test does not exercise the reported bug or the fixed-host round-robin case
findings.body: The added test only checks that the same UTC slots are returned for a +6:00 invitee, with the comment saying the result should match UTC. It does not cover an organizer timezone different from the schedule timezone, a round-robin event with a fixed host override, or a busy calendar event that should block a slot on an override day. The round-robin fixed-host behaviour and the busy-time bypass introduced in slots.ts are not tested.
